title: TSMC OIP Ecosystem Forum 2026: Broadcom’s View of ASICs and Ecosystems - Semiwiki
gist: SemiWiki recap of Broadcom's TSMC OIP 2026 keynote (Greg Dix): Broadcom aims to be an 'enduring incumbent' in custom XPUs by betting early on technologies with TSMC, pre-validating 3D integration via test vehicles for first-time-right silicon. A recent large XPU went kickoff-to-tapeout in about nine months, and AI-driven design will compress schedules further.

insights.claim: Broadcom has long been the ASIC supplier to beat because of a vast library of proven IP, especially SerDes, plus deep design skills inherited from the LSI Logic acquisition.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Supports Broadcom's durable leadership in custom AI XPU programs.

insights.claim: Broadcom's goal is to be an 'enduring incumbent': a supplier can win once on aggressive schedule, technology or price, but winning repeatedly requires execution.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Repeat XPU program wins create sticky, recurring custom-silicon revenue.
insights.quote: A supplier can win once by promising an aggressive schedule, technology, or price. Winning repeatedly requires something harder, execution.
insights.locator: The objective is not merely to win

insights.claim: Because new semiconductor technologies take two to three years to develop and qualify, Broadcom places multiple technology bets in parallel and abandons those that fail to deliver value.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Scale to fund parallel R&D bets is a barrier to entry for smaller ASIC houses.

insights.claim: Broadcom has shifted from fast follower to early adopter, working with TSMC on technologies while still evolving, which lets it shape emerging technologies around future products.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Deepening Broadcom-TSMC co-development raises switching costs for hyperscaler XPU customers.

insights.claim: Broadcom sees 3D die stacking as the next major step in AI processors, beyond multi-die assemblies with I/O chiplets, HBM and interposers.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Signals rising demand for advanced packaging (e.g., TSMC SoIC/3D) and associated EDA/test.

insights.claim: 3D stacking introduces new problems in multi-layer power delivery, heat extraction, cross-node timing analysis, known-good-die testing and a big increase in design compute.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Thermal, power-delivery and test vendors gain content in 3D AI chips.
insights.locator: Stacking dies introduces an entirely new

insights.claim: Broadcom runs mechanical, thermal, electrical and risk-mitigation test vehicles ahead of production to achieve first-time-right silicon, studying warpage, thermal, SerDes, HBM and routing.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Pre-validation capability is a moat in large-die AI ASICs.

insights.claim: For today's largest AI accelerators, a silicon re-spin can mean missing the market entirely, not just an engineering delay.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Execution risk is binary for XPU programs; incumbents with track records are favored.

insights.claim: A recent large Broadcom XPU program went from kickoff to tapeout in roughly nine months.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Faster cycles mean hyperscaler custom silicon refreshes more often, boosting ASIC volume.
insights.locator: Greg pointed to a recent large XPU

insights.claim: Broadcom expects AI-driven design to further compress implementation schedules, increasing pressure on backend design, verification, compute infrastructure and methodology.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Tailwind for AI-enabled EDA tools and design compute.

insights.claim: Development is becoming concurrent, with process, packaging, IP, tools and customer products evolving at the same time rather than sequentially, requiring close collaboration across foundries, memory, OSATs, EDA and equipment vendors.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Ecosystem-integrated players (TSMC OIP partners) benefit; isolated designers lose.
